extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the GAP computer algebra system (mathematicians/computational algebra programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for cyclotomic numbers, floating-point and boolean behaviours in GAP: definitions, function semantics, representation choices, and package interface requirements. Covers function-level contracts, ordering/comparison rules, conversion semantics, and warnings about performance and numerical precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoeffsCyc external representation
rubrics_metrics.description: CoeffsCyc(cyc, N) returns a list of length N whose j-th entry equals the coefficient of exp(2πi(j-1)/N) if that root belongs to the N-th Zumbroich basis, and zero otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to form an external representation of a cyclotomic; examples show how to read coefficients and that CoeffsCyc may return different lists for different N (e.g., conductor versus larger N).

rubrics_metrics.name: DenominatorCyc
rubrics_metrics.description: DenominatorCyc(cyc) returns the smallest positive integer n such that n * cyc is a cyclotomic integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rational cyc the result equals DenominatorRat; use to determine scaling to integral cyclotomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtRepOfObj for cyclotomics
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtRepOfObj(cyc) returns the external representation of a cyclotomic cyc with conductor n: the list returned by CoeffsCyc(cyc, n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the canonical external list representation for a cyclotomic's conductor.

rubrics_metrics.name: DescriptionOfRootOfUnity
rubrics_metrics.description: DescriptionOfRootOfUnity(root) returns [n,e] of coprime positive integers such that root = E(n)^e, assuming the argument is indeed a root of unity (this is not checked).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function does not verify root-of-unity property; callers should ensure preconditions hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGaussInt predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGaussInt(x) returns true iff x is a Gaussian integer, i.e., of the form a + b*E(4) with integers a,b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test membership in GaussianIntegers; false otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsGaussRat predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: IsGaussRat(x) returns true iff x is a Gaussian rational, i.e., a + b*E(4) with rationals a,b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to test membership in GaussianRationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: DefaultField for cyclotomics
rubrics_metrics.description: DefaultField(list) returns the smallest cyclotomic field containing the given elements (as opposed to Field which returns the smallest field, not necessarily cyclotomic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields represent vector spaces over Q; DefaultField ensures returned field is cyclotomic when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity objects and behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: infinity and -infinity are special GAP objects in CyclotomicsFamily representing elements larger/smaller than all others; used as return values for Size or Dimension for infinite cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They lie in IsInfinity but not IsCyc (so one can distinguish them); arithmetic with them is provided for convenience (e.g., -infinity + 1 = -infinity). Beware membership tests and comparisons involving infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic comparison ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison operators (<, <=, =, >=, >, <>) on cyclotomics follow: rationals compared naturally; rationals < irrational cyclotomics; among irrational cyclotomics with different conductors, smaller conductor is considered smaller; with same conductor compare via external representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex conjugation and Galois automorphisms interact with comparisons; see ExtRepOfObj and Conductor for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic ATLAS irrationalities (EB..EH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions EB(N), EC(N), ED(N), EE(N), EF(N), EG(N), EH(N) produce so-called atomic irrationalities bN,cN,dN,eN,... defined as specific sums of z^{j^k} with congruence conditions on N (e.g., N ≡ 1 (mod k) for k=2..8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EC..EH require N to be prime. Values may be rational for some N; examples illustrate usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: EI and ER square-root irrationalities
rubrics_metrics.description: ER(N) returns sqrt(N) following GAP embedding conventions; EI(N) = E(4) * ER(N). For rational N, ER is installed as method for Sqrt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign conventions chosen via embedding into C: ER returns positive sqrt for positive N; for negative N, ER(N) = EI(-N). Gauss formulas relate these to EB values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum-type irrationalities (EY..ES, EM..EJ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions EY, EX, EW, EV, EU, ET, ES and EM, EL, EK, EJ construct algebraic numbers defined as truncated sums z + z^n + z^{n^2} + ... (with signs for EM..EJ) where n = N_k defined per Section NK and based on multiplicative orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-argument versions (with d) use NK to choose the appropriate exponent n; examples show concrete outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NK selection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: NK(N,k,d) returns the (d+1)-th integer with multiplicative order exactly k modulo N chosen according to a fixed preference ordering; if no such integer exists NK returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NK underlies the two-argument versions of many atomic irrationality constructors (EY(N,d) etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: AtlasIrrationality string syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: AtlasIrrationality(irratname) parses strings describing linear combinations of atomic irrationalities using an 'ampersand' syntax where '&k' denotes a conjugate q*_k and multiplication, addition, and conjugation scopes are specified (coefficients scope broken by + or - but not by &).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show parsing results; useful for entering ATLAS-style irrational combinations concisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisCyc operation
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisCyc(cyc,k) returns the cyclotomic obtained by raising roots of unity in the Zumbroich-basis representation of cyc to the k-th power; if k is coprime to conductor n this acts as a Galois automorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ComplexConjugate(z) = GaloisCyc(z,-1). GaloisCyc can be applied elementwise to lists/matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComplexConjugate, RealPart, ImaginaryPart semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ComplexConjugate(z) returns GaloisCyc(z,-1) for cyclotomics or appropriate quaternion conjugates; RealPart(z) and ImaginaryPart(z) return (z + ComplexConjugate(z))/2 and (z - ComplexConjugate(z))/2i respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applied to lists, operation is elementwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: StarCyc for quadratic conjugate
rubrics_metrics.description: StarCyc(cyc) returns the unique Galois conjugate different from cyc when cyc is an irrational element of a quadratic extension of Q; otherwise it returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to obtain the other root in quadratic extensions; returns fail for non-quadratic or rational cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic decomposition of cyclotomics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quadratic(cyc) returns a record {a,b,root,d,ATLAS,display} if cyc is a cyclotomic integer lying in a quadratic extension, representing cyc = (a + b*sqrt(root))/d with constraints on d (1 or 2) and canonical ATLAS/display forms; returns fail otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If d=2 additional format rules apply (n ≡ 1 (mod 4) etc.); the ATLAS component is a representation in terms of atomic irrationalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: GaloisMat orbit computation
rubrics_metrics.description: GaloisMat(mat) computes complete orbits of rows of a matrix of cyclotomics under the Galois group action and returns a record with components mat (rows grouped by orbits), galoisfams (encoding orbit info), and generators (permutations generating the action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: galoisfams entries explained: 1 for rationals, -1 for unknowns, [l1,l2] for first element of orbit with positions and automorphisms, 0 for non-first orbit members. Identical rows cause a warning and are only considered once.

rubrics_metrics.name: RationalizedMat traces over orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: RationalizedMat(mat) returns the list of rationalized rows of mat, i.e., the sums over Galois orbits of entries (a trace-like operation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No two input rows should be equal; useful to obtain rational combinations from orbit sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internally represented cyclotomics design tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Internally represented cyclotomics are implemented as lists of length equal to their conductor (internal representation refers to smallest cyclotomic field containing the element), making embedding and constructing sums/products across cyclotomic fields easy, but arithmetic becomes expensive (many coefficients) and memory-consuming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not recommended for heavy arithmetic over number fields (e.g., matrix computations); consider AlgebraicExtension to work in small extension fields when embeddings are not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomics conductor limit and tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a limit on the conductor of internally represented cyclotomics (default 1,000,000) to avoid excessive computation/memory use; maximum depends on machine word size (2^28-1 on 32-bit, 2^32-1 on 64-bit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SetCyclotomicsLimit(newlimit) to increase the limit (cannot lower it) and GetCyclotomicsLimit() to query; raising the limit may make computations slow or memory-heavy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floats: numerical precision caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating-point numbers in GAP are approximate and do not form a ring in the strict GAP sense; numerical imprecision means many GAP algorithms expecting exact algebraic objects are not applicable to floats (e.g., GCD doesn't make sense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful mixing numerical and algebraic code; comparisons between floats and rationals are forbidden by design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floating-point literal/input rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating-point literals must contain a decimal digit ('.1', '.1e1', '-.999' are valid). An underscore suffix (e.g., 1._) forces immediate conversion to the current floating-point format; optional one-letter specifies handler/precision (default handler letter 'l').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literals are stored as strings and converted upon first use, so raising precision later will cause re-evaluation of constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float creator semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Float(obj) creates a floating-point number from a rational, string, or existing float; it chooses precision so that Int(Float(obj)) = obj for integers and usually enough precision to convert back to the original rational; options allow specifying PrecisionFloat := prec bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewFloat(filter,obj) and MakeFloat(sample,obj) provide alternate construction; Float(obj:PrecisionFloat:=1000) creates high-precision approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rat for floats: rational approximation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Rat(f) returns a rational approximation to floating-point f; optional controls Rat(f:maxdenom:=md,maxpartial:=mp) constrain the denominator <= md and continued fraction partials <= mp; defaults are maxpartial:=10000 and maxdenom:=2^(precision/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No guarantee to recover original rational, but returns the most ‘reasonable’ given f's precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyc for floats: cyclotomic approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyc(f[,degree]) constructs a cyclotomic approximation to floating-point f (optionally bounded by degree) using LLL lattice reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not guaranteed to recover original algebraic object; returns a best-fit cyclotomic of controlled degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetFloats: installing float handlers
rubrics_metrics.description: SetFloats(rec[,bits][,install]) installs a new interface to floating-point numbers in GAP; optional bits specify desired precision in binary digits; install boolean=false installs handler without making it default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by packages implementing arbitrary-precision floats; see high-precision package interface requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLOAT constants record
rubrics_metrics.description: The global record FLOAT contains floating-point constants such as MANT_DIG (mantissa bits), VIEW_DIG (digits to display), PI, EPSILON, INFINITY, NAN, and others matching C names (without DBL_ or M_ prefixes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect FLOAT to query handler-specific constants; used by floating-point implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EqFloat equality semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: EqFloat(x,y) compares two floats and returns true iff they are equal, with the special rule that NaN is always considered different from itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EqFloat instead of = when comparing floats because IEEE754 NaN would violate GAP's requirement that every object be equal to itself if = were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrecisionFloat attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: PrecisionFloat(x) returns the precision of floating-point number x measured in binary digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to inspect and control numeric precision for created floats.

rubrics_metrics.name: SignBit and SignFloat
rubrics_metrics.description: SignBit(x) returns boolean sign bit true if x is negative (including -0.); SignFloat(x) returns -1 if x<0, 0 if x=0, 1 if x>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes signed zero and sign semantics of floats.

rubrics_metrics.name: SinCos convenience function
rubrics_metrics.description: SinCos(x) returns the list [sin(x), cos(x)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small convenience to compute sin and cos together (likely more efficient than separate calls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Atan2 polar angle semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Atan2(y,x) returns the polar angle (principal value) of (x,y) in (-π,π], undefined at (0,0); defined in accordance with IEEE 1788-2015 and imported from IEEE 754.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for robust argument computation respecting IEEE standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log1p and Expm1 inverse relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Log1p(x) returns ln(1+x) and Expm1(x) returns exp(x)-1; the two functions are inverses of each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for improved precision for small x where direct log(1+x) or exp(x)-1 lose precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erf definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Erf(x) returns the error function given by (2/sqrt(pi)) * integral_0^x exp(-t^2) dt, imported from IEEE 754.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available as a standard floating-point special function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity / NaN testers for floats
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPInfinity(x), IsNInfinity(x), IsXInfinity(x), IsFinite(x), IsNaN(x) return true iff x is respectively +∞, -∞, ±∞, finite, or NaN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these filters to guard operations sensitive to infinities or NaNs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard math operations for floats
rubrics_metrics.description: A large set of standard mathematical functions are provided for floats (Sin,Cos,Tan,...,Sinh,Cosh,...,Log,Log2,Log10,Exp,Exp2,Exp10,CubeRoot,Square,Hypothenuse,Ceil,Floor,Round,Trunc,FrExp,LdExp,AbsoluteValue,Norm,Frac,Zeta,Gamma etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions named with numerals indicate base (e.g., Log2 base 2); Log/Exp use natural base e.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-precision float package interface requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A package implementing high-precision floats must provide a record with optional fields creator, eager, objbyextrep, filter, constants; must install methods Int,Rat,String for its objects and creators NewFloat(filter,IsRat), NewFloat(IsString), and must install methods for arithmetic and numerical operations (SUM, Exp, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User selects implementation by calling SetFloats with the package record (and optional precision). The package constants should include MANT_DIG, MAX, MIN, NAN, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex float support expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex arithmetic may be provided by packages (e.g., float). Complex numbers may be input with 'i' and created via NewFloat with three arguments (filter, real, imag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package should implement Norm, RealPart, ImaginaryPart, ComplexConjugate and related methods to treat complex floats as usual numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument for complex floats
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument(z) returns the argument of complex number z computed as Atan2(ImaginaryPart(z),RealPart(z)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides principal argument for complex floats consistent with Atan2 orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interval arithmetic semantics and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interval arithmetic packages implement intervals as sets [a,b] with comparisons defined componentwise ([a,b] ≤ [c,d] iff a ≤ c and b ≤ d). Standard interval operations: Sup (supremum), Inf (infimum), Mid (midpoint), AbsoluteDiameter (Sup-Inf), RelativeDiameter ((Sup-Inf)/|Min(x)|), IsDisjoint, IsSubset, IncreaseInterval (increase absolute diameter), BlowupInterval (increase relative diameter), BisectInterval (bisect interval into two).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interval comparison semantics (overlap/containment) are important design choices; use provided operations to manage interval widths and testing relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean values and IsBool
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal boolean values are true and false; fail is also treated as a boolean for technical reasons. IsBool(obj) tests whether obj is true, false, or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convention: predicate functions that return true/false begin with Is; fail is a special value indicating operation failure and behaves differently from true/false in boolean contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: fail semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The global value fail indicates that an operation could not be performed for given arguments (computability/implementation restrictions). fail is an object distinct from all others and is treated technically as a boolean but cannot be used in boolean lists or in boolean expressions with and/or/not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many GAP operations return fail to signal inability rather than raise errors; code should explicitly test for fail when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean equality and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality = between booleans returns true if both are the same (true/false/fail); inequality <> is exclusive-or. Ordering is defined true < false < fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons with objects of other types yield false for equality. Use ordering only in contexts that expect it; be mindful of fail's place as largest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical disjunction (or) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator 'or' evaluates first operand; if it is neither true nor false an error is signalled. If first operand is true, 'or' returns true without evaluating second operand (short-circuit). If first is false, second is evaluated (and must be true or false). 'or' is associative and has lowest precedence among logical operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-circuiting is important to avoid evaluating expressions that may be expensive or cause errors; examples illustrate guarding index access with 'or'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical conjunction (and) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator 'and' returns true iff both operands are true and false otherwise; it short-circuits evaluation (first operand evaluated first; if it is neither true nor false an error is signalled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-circuiting allows safe guarding of potentially invalid expressions; use 'and' to avoid unnecessary evaluation.
